newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador economic team to remain intact -- Jaramillo.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador economic team to remain intact -- Jaramillo.

text.p: Ecuador's economic team will remain the same after President Fabian Alarcon announced his new cabinet on Monday, said the head of the country's central bank Fidel Jaramillo.
"The cabinet was confirmed today, including the existing economic team," Jaramillo told reporters here.
The confirmation put to rest speculation some members of the current economic team would be replaced. Jaramillo said the economic group headed by Finance Minister Carlos Davalos would stay intact.
On Ecuador's economic outlook, Jaramillo said the government target of public defict equal to about 2.7 percent of Gross Domestic Product seemed achievable in 1997.
"My personal feeling is that so far it is attainable," he said.
Jaramillo also said Ecuador was in "fiscal equilibrium" in the first four months of the year, coming off a deficit of 3.0 percent of GDP in 1996.
Jaramillo said President Alarcon would annouce a finalized austerity plan in the coming weeks. The measures will add to current efforts aimed at shoring up the country's fiscal deficit, he said.
Also present at the press conference, Finance Ministry official Mauricio Pareja said Ecuador is expected to reach a stand-by loan agreement with the International Monetary fund (IMF) later this year.
"We would expect to reach an agreement with the IMF by October, maybe November," Pareja said.
The stand-by agreement is seen as helping to pave the way for Ecuador to clinch a debt rescheduling accord with the Paris Club.
Ecuador is in arrears on about $250 million of principal owed on its $1.2 billion Paris Club debt. Ecuador made a payment of $33 million in past due interest to the Club last week, Jaramillo said.
